questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design multi-cluster deployment pipelines in Azure DevOps, combining GitOps (Flux) and traditional Helm approaches. It evaluates understanding of per-cluster configuration management, secrets handling, progressive delivery strategies, and observability—all critical skills for production-grade Kubernetes deployments.

## Key Concepts
- Azure DevOps YAML templates with conditional stages and jobs
- Flux GitOps vs Helm deployments in AKS clusters
- Azure App Configuration for feature flags per cluster
- Azure Key Vault secrets integration
- Canary deployments and health checks
- Azure Policy gates and automatic rollback strategies
- Azure Monitor Logs for pipeline observability

## Code Example
```yaml
# azure-pipelines.yml
trigger:
  - main

resources:
  repositories:
    - repository: templates
      type: git
      name: Shared/PipelineTemplates

parameters:
  - name: environments
    type: object
    default:
      - name: dev
        cluster: dev-aks-eastus
        clusterType: flux
      - name: staging
        cluster: staging-aks-eastus
        clusterType: helm
      - name: prod
        cluster: prod-aks-westeu
        clusterType: helm

stages:
  - stage: Build
    jobs:
      - job: BuildAndPush
        steps:
          - task: Docker@2
            displayName: Build and push container
            inputs:
              containerRegistry: 'acrConnection'
              repository: 'myapp'
              tag: '$(Build.BuildId)'

  - stage: Deploy_Dev
    dependsOn: Build
    jobs:
      - template: deploy-aks.yml@templates
        parameters:
          environment: dev
          clusterName: dev-aks-eastus
          clusterType: flux
          appConfigName: app-config-dev
          keyVaultName: kv-dev-eastus

  - stage: Deploy_Staging
    dependsOn: Deploy_Dev
    jobs:
      - template: deploy-aks.yml@templates
        parameters:
          environment: staging
          clusterName: staging-aks-eastus
          clusterType: helm
          appConfigName: app-config-staging
          keyVaultName: kv-staging-eastus
      - job: CanaryHealthCheck
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az aks command invoke \
                  --name staging-aks-eastus \
                  --resource-group rg-staging \
                  --command "kubectl rollout status deployment/myapp"

  - stage: Deploy_Prod
    dependsOn: Deploy_Staging
    jobs:
      - deployment: DeployProd
        environment: 'prod'
        strategy:
          runOnce:
            deploy:
              steps:
                - template: deploy-aks.yml@templates
                  parameters:
                    environment: prod
                    clusterName: prod-aks-westeu
                    clusterType: helm
                    appConfigName: app-config-prod
                    keyVaultName: kv-prod-westeu
      - job: ProdGate
        dependsOn: DeployProd
        steps:
          - task: AzurePolicy@0
            displayName: Check production policy compliance
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
              policyDefinition: 'prod-aks-policy'
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: Verify health and rollback if failed
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                HEALTH=$(curl -s http://myapp.prod.internal/health)
                if [ "$HEALTH" != "healthy" ]; then
                  echo "##vso[task.logissue type=error]Health check failed"
                  echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=ROLLBACK;isOutput=true]true"
                  exit 1
                fi

  - stage: Monitor
    dependsOn:
      - Deploy_Dev
      - Deploy_Staging
      - Deploy_Prod
    jobs:
      - job: LogToMonitor
        steps:
          - task: AzureCLI@2
            displayName: Log deployment results to Azure Monitor
            inputs:
              azureSubscription: 'monitorConnection'
              scriptType: 'bash'
              scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
              inlineScript: |
                az monitor app-insights trace show \
                  --app myapp-insights \
                  --analytics "deployment | where timestamp > ago(1h)"
```

```yaml
# deploy-aks.yml (template)
parameters:
  - name: environment
    type: string
  - name: clusterName
    type: string
  - name: clusterType
    type: string
  - name: appConfigName
    type: string
  - name: keyVaultName
    type: string

steps:
  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: 'Fetch App Configuration flags for ${{ parameters.environment }}'
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
      scriptType: 'bash'
      scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
      inlineScript: |
        az appconfig kv export \
          --name ${{ parameters.appConfigName }} \
          --format json \
          --output-file config.json

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: 'Fetch Key Vault secrets for ${{ parameters.environment }}'
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
      scriptType: 'bash'
      scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
      inlineScript: |
        az keyvault secret list \
          --vault-name ${{ parameters.keyVaultName }} \
          --query '[].name' \
          -o tsv

  - task: HelmDeploy@0
    displayName: 'Deploy to ${{ parameters.clusterName }}'
    condition: eq('${{ parameters.clusterType }}', 'helm')
    inputs:
      connectionType: 'Azure Resource Manager'
      azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
      azureResourceGroup: 'rg-aks'
      kubernetesCluster: '${{ parameters.clusterName }}'
      namespace: '${{ parameters.environment }}'
      command: 'upgrade --install'
      chartType: 'FilePath'
      chartPath: 'charts/myapp'
      valueFile: 'charts/myapp/values-${{ parameters.environment }}.yaml'

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: 'Deploy via Flux for GitOps cluster'
    condition: eq('${{ parameters.clusterType }}', 'flux')
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: 'aksConnection'
      scriptType: 'bash'
      scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
      inlineScript: |
        az aks get-credentials --name ${{ parameters.clusterName }} --resource-group rg-aks
        flux install
        flux create source git myapp \
          --url=https://github.com/org/repo \
          --branch=main
        flux create kustomization myapp \
          --source=myapp \
          --path=clusters/${{ parameters.environment }}
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Ephemeral PR environments are a cornerstone of modern DevOps practices, enabling teams to validate changes in isolated environments without affecting production. This question assesses the candidate's understanding of Kubernetes lifecycle management, infrastructure-as-code practices, and observability in cloud-native deployments.

## Key Concepts
- PR-triggered ephemeral environments for isolated testing
- Kubernetes namespaces dynamically provisioned per PR
- Helm-based application deployments
- End-to-end smoke testing in isolated environments
- Automated teardown with policy safeguards and comprehensive logging

## Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none
pr:
  branches:
    include:
    - main
  paths:
    include:
    - src/**
    - charts/**
    - azure-pipelines.yml

variables:
  PR_NUMBER: $(System.PullRequest.PullRequestNumber)
  NAMESPACE: 'pr-$(PR_NUMBER)'
  RETENTION_HOURS: 24
  AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION: 'Azure-Production'
  AKS_CLUSTER: 'aks-cluster-01'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: 'rg-aks-prod'

stages:
- stage: Provision
  displayName: 'Provision Ephemeral Environment'
  jobs:
  - job: CreateNamespace
    displayName: 'Create PR Namespace'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Create AKS Namespace'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az aks get-credentials \
            --resource-group $(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
            --name $(AKS_CLUSTER) \
            --overwrite-existing
          
          kubectl create namespace $(NAMESPACE) --dry-run=client -o yaml | \
            kubectl apply -f -
          
          kubectl label namespace $(NAMESPACE) \
            pr.number=$(PR_NUMBER) \
            pr.created=$(Build.BuildNumber) \
            environment=ephemeral --overwrite
          
          echo "##vso[task.setvariable variable=NAMESPACE;isOutput=true]$(NAMESPACE)"
      name: namespaceInfo

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Log to Azure Monitor'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az monitor log-analytics query \
            --workspace $(LOG_WORKSPACE_ID) \
            --query "['EphemeralEnvironmentCreated']" \
            --analytics-duration 1 | tee /dev/stderr

- stage: Deploy
  displayName: 'Deploy Application'
  dependsOn: Provision
  jobs:
  - job: HelmDeploy
    displayName: 'Deploy with Helm'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: HelmInstaller@1
      displayName: 'Install Helm'
      inputs:
        helmVersionToInstall: 'latest'

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Configure AKS Credentials'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az aks get-credentials \
            --resource-group $(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
            --name $(AKS_CLUSTER) \
            --overwrite-existing

    - task: HelmDeploy@0
      displayName: 'Deploy Helm Chart'
      inputs:
        connectionType: 'Azure Resource Manager'
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        azureResourceGroup: '$(RESOURCE_GROUP)'
        kubernetesCluster: '$(AKS_CLUSTER)'
        namespace: '$(NAMESPACE)'
        chartName: '$(CHART_REPO)/$(CHART_NAME)'
        chartVersion: '$(Build.BuildNumber)'
        releaseName: 'pr-app-$(PR_NUMBER)'
        overrideValues: |
          image.tag=$(Build.BuildNumber)
          ingress.hostname=$(NAMESPACE).$(DOMAIN)

- stage: Test
  displayName: 'Smoke Tests'
  dependsOn: Deploy
  jobs:
  - job: SmokeTests
    displayName: 'Run Smoke Tests'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Wait for Deployment'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          kubectl wait --for=condition=available \
            --timeout=300s \
            deployment/pr-app-$(PR_NUMBER) \
            -n $(NAMESPACE)

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Run Smoke Tests'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          SERVICE_IP=$(kubectl get svc -n $(NAMESPACE) \
            -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}')
          
          curl -f http://$SERVICE_IP/health || exit 1
          curl -f http://$SERVICE_IP/api/version || exit 1

- stage: Teardown
  displayName: 'Teardown Environment'
  condition: or(
    eq(variables['Build.Reason'], 'PullRequest'),
    eq(dependencies.Provision.outputs['CreateNamespace.namespaceInfo.namespace'], '')
  )
  jobs:
  - job: DeleteNamespace
    displayName: 'Delete PR Namespace'
    pool:
      vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'
    steps:
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Policy Check Before Deletion'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          NAMESPACE=$(NAMESPACE)
          if [[ "$NAMESPACE" == pr-* ]]; then
            echo "Validating deletion policy for ephemeral namespace..."
            az policy assignment list \
              --scope /subscriptions/$(SUB_ID)/resourceGroups/$(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
              --query "[?displayName=='ProtectEphemeralNamespaces']" | tee /dev/stderr
          else
            echo "##vso[task.logissue type=warning]Non-PR namespace - skipping deletion"
            exit 1
          fi

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Delete Namespace'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          kubectl delete namespace $(NAMESPACE) --wait=true
          
          echo "Namespace $(NAMESPACE) deleted successfully"

    - task: AzureCLI@2
      displayName: 'Log Deletion to Azure Monitor'
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '$(AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        scriptLocation: 'inlineScript'
        inlineScript: |
          az monitor metrics alert create \
            --name "namespace-deleted-$(NAMESPACE)" \
            --resource-group $(RESOURCE_GROUP) \
            --description "Ephemeral namespace $(NAMESPACE) has been deleted"

resources:
  webhooks:
  - webhook: PRClosed
    connectionType: 'azureDevOps'
    project: '$(System.TeamProject)'
    pipeline: '$(Build.DefinitionName)'

schedules:
- cron: '0 0 * * *'
  displayName: 'Daily Cleanup'
  branches:
    include:
    - main
  always: true
```

## Key Implementation Details
1. **Namespace Creation**: Dynamically creates pr-${PR_NUMBER} namespace with metadata labels for tracking
2. **Helm Deployment**: Uses HelmDeploy@0 task with Azure Resource Manager connection for secure deployment
3. **Smoke Testing**: Validates application health and API endpoints post-deployment
4. **Policy Protection**: Validates namespace pattern before deletion to prevent accidental removal of non-prod environments
5. **Azure Monitor Logging**: All operations are logged for audit and troubleshooting
6. **Scheduled Cleanup**: Cron job ensures stale environments are removed after 24 hours
7. **Webhook Integration**: Triggers cleanup when PR is merged or closed

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This evaluates foundational CI/CD knowledge including pipeline configuration, artifact management, and release governance with security controls.

## Key Concepts
- Azure Pipelines YAML configuration and triggers
- Python environment setup with version 3.11
- Test execution with pytest and coverage reporting
- Wheel package building and artifact publishing
- Release environments with manual approval gates
- Security scanning integration for production deployments

## Code Example
```yaml
# Azure Pipelines YAML for Python CI/CD
trigger:
  - main
pr:
  - main

pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'

variables:
  pythonVersion: '3.11'

stages:
- stage: Build
  displayName: 'Build and Test Stage'
  jobs:
  - job: BuildJob
    displayName: 'Build and Test'
    steps:
    - task: UsePythonVersion@0
      inputs:
        versionSpec: '$(pythonVersion)'
      displayName: 'Use Python $(pythonVersion)'
    
    - script: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install -r requirements.txt
        pip install pytest pytest-cov
      displayName: 'Install dependencies'
    
    - script: |
        pytest --cov=. --cov-report=xml --cov-report=html
      displayName: 'Run tests with coverage'
    
    - script: |
        python setup.py bdist_wheel
      displayName: 'Build wheel package'
    
    - task: PublishBuildArtifacts@1
      inputs:
        pathToPublish: 'dist'
        artifactName: 'python-wheel'
      displayName: 'Publish wheel artifact'

- stage: Release
  displayName: 'Release to Production'
  dependsOn: Build
  condition: succeeded()
  jobs:
```

Code Example
```yaml
trigger: none
pr: none
pr:
  branches:
    include: ['*']
variables:
  azureSubscription: 'YOUR-SERVICE-CONNECTION'
  infraDir: 'infra'
stages:
- stage: Provision
  jobs:
  - job: Terraform
    steps:
    - task: Checkout@1
    - script: |
        terraform init
        terraform apply -auto-approve
      workingDirectory: $(infraDir)
- stage: Deploy
  dependsOn: Provision
  jobs:
  - job: DeployAPI
    steps:
    - task: HelmDeploy@0
      inputs:
        connectionType: 'Azure Resource Manager'
        kubernetesServiceConnection: 'AKS-Connection'
        namespace: 'default'
        releaseName: 'api-pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)'
        chartType: 'FilePath'
        chartPath: './charts/api'
    - task: AzureAppConfiguration@1
      inputs:
        connectedService: '$(azureSubscription)'
        action: 'getKeyValues'
        keyValues: 'perPRFlags'
    - task: AzureKeyVault@2

        connectedServiceName: '$(azureSubscription)'
        vaultName: 'my-vault'
        secretsFilter: 'PR_$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId)*'
- stage: TestAndHealth
  dependsOn: Deploy
  jobs:
  - job: HealthCheck
    steps:
    - script: |
        curl -sSf http://api-pr-$(System.PullRequest.PullRequestId).ingress | grep 'OK'
      displayName: 'Health check'
- stage: Teardown
  condition: always()
  jobs:
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests a realistic, beginner-friendly pipeline that covers core Azure DevOps tasks: CI, Docker, ACR, App Service slots, App Configuration integration, health-based swap, and Log Analytics auditing.

## Key Concepts

- YAML pipelines and multi-stage design
- Docker build/push to Azure Container Registry
- Azure App Service deployment slots (staging/production) and slot swap
- Azure App Configuration for per-environment flags
- Health checks and rollback strategies
- Logging/auditing to Azure Monitor / Log Analytics
- Service connections and least-privilege access

## Code Example

```yaml
trigger:
- main
pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest
variables:
  imageName: myapi
  registry: <ACR_NAME>.azurecr.io
stages:
- stage: Build
  jobs:
  - job: Test
    steps:
    - task: NodeTool@0
      inputs: {version: '18.x'}
    - script: npm install
    - script: npm test
- stage: Deploy
  jobs:
  - job: Deploy
    steps:
    - task: Docker@2
      inputs:
        command: buildAndPush
        containerRegistry: '<registry-service-connection>'
        repository: '$(registry)/$(imageName)'
        Dockerfile: '**/Dockerfile'
        tags: |
          $(Build.BuildId)
    - task: AzureWebAppContainer@1
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '<subscription-connection>'
        appName: '<app-service-name>'
        imageName: '$(registry)/$(imageName):$(Build.BuildId)'
        resourceGroup: '<rg>'
        slotName: 'staging'
    - task: AzureCLI@2
      inputs:
        azureSubscription: '<subscription-connection>'
        scriptType: 'bash'
        script: |
          HEALTH_URL=https://<app-service-name>-staging.azurewebsites.net/health
          if curl -sSf $HEALTH_URL | grep -q 'ok'; then
            az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app-service-name> --slot staging --target-slot production
          else
            az webapp deployment slot swap --resource-group <rg> --name <app-service-name> --slot production --target-slot staging
            exit 1
          fi
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you add a retry policy for the health check without masking failures?
- How would you extend this to support a blue/green rollout for multiple regions?
